headline.purpose: Every page's own <h1>. Identical everywhere on purpose — a page never invents its own hero size.

body.purpose: Default running text size across the whole app — table cells, inputs, most copy.

label.purpose: Column headers, section eyebrows, and status/stage badge text.

stat.purpose: Large glanceable numerals in a dashboard stat tile. Deliberately close to Headline's 28px but a separate role — data being scanned, not a page title.

shadows.name: 2xs
shadows.purpose: Default resting shadow for most content cards.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: A card that wants slightly more separation from the ground.

shadows.name: md
shadows.purpose: Reserved for elements clearly floating above the page.

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Open dialogs and sheets above their scrim.

shadows.name: xl
shadows.purpose: The heaviest tier — rare, for the most prominent floating surface on screen.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition easing (color/box-shadow state changes, dialog fade+zoom).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one call-to-action per view. Apple System Blue fill, white text.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary"><svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="12" y1="5" x2="12" y2="19"/><line x1="5" y1="12" x2="19" y2="12"/></svg>New Project</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 15px; background: #0071e3; color: #ffffff; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), opacity 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary .ds-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(0,113,227,0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A second-priority action beside a primary one.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 15px; background: #e8e8ed; color: #1d1d1f; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #dcdce2; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(0,113,227,0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Delete/cancel confirmations only — never used for an ordinary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 15px; background: #ff3b30; color: #ffffff; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255,59,48,0.3); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Stage Badge
components.description: A pipeline stage or status marker — the same stage always renders the same color everywhere.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; width: fit-content; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(0,113,227,0.15); color: #0058b5; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Hairline border at rest, blue ring on focus — same focus language as buttons.

narrative.overview:
Lampara CRM is a tool run all day, at a desk and on a job site — not a marketing surface. The system stays restrained and high-trust: a cool grey-white ground, solid white panels that separate by soft shadow rather than a border, and exactly one accent color used sparingly. Nothing announces itself; everything is legible at a glance across a long shift.

Frost (backdrop-filter: blur) is reserved for the few places layers genuinely overlap — a sticky nav bar, a dialog's scrim, a popover floating over local content — never applied to a plain content panel. Elevation stays quiet and mostly structural: shadows exist for real separation and real state changes (hover, an open dialog), not as decoration layered onto every surface by default.

This is explicitly not: warm or cream "AI-generated" tones, purple gradients, heavy borders standing in for shadow, or color used decoratively to fill space. The body of the interface is grayscale; color is reserved for the one accent, for status (destructive red), and for the handful of semantic stage/status badges the pipeline itself defines.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey-white ground (#f5f5f7), never warm or cream
One accent color (Apple System Blue) — hairline-restrained hierarchy does the rest
Panels separate from the ground by shadow, not border; hairline borders are for dividers within a panel
Frost only where layers actually overlap (nav, dialog, popover) — never on plain content
Full light/dark theming, remapped 1:1 onto the same semantic tokens

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Apple System Blue is the only color used to mean "this is clickable and important." Everything else — status badges, stage colors — is a semantic color, never a second brand accent competing with blue for attention.

rules.name: The Shadow-Not-Border Rule
rules.body: A card separates from the page by shadow. A hairline border is only for a divider inside a panel — never for the panel's own outer edge.

rules.name: The One Headline Rule
rules.body: Every page's top-level heading uses the exact same 28px/700/-0.02em treatment. A page never invents its own hero size.

rules.name: The Smallest-Tier-First Rule
rules.body: Reach for shadow-2xs/shadow-sm by default. A heavier tier is a deliberate choice for something genuinely floating above the page (a dialog, a FAB), not a way to make an ordinary card feel more important.

dos: Do use exactly one accent color (Apple System Blue) for anything meant to read as "clickable and important."
Do separate a panel from the page with shadow, reserving hairline borders for dividers within a panel.
Do reach for the smallest shadow tier that does the job; save the heavier tiers for things genuinely floating above the page (dialogs, popovers, a FAB).
Do keep every page's <h1> at the same 28px/700/-0.02em treatment — this consistency is a feature, not an oversight to "improve."
Do apply frost (backdrop-filter) only to a fixed/sticky element that has real scrolling or stacked content moving underneath it.
Do give every pipeline stage and status its own fixed, consistent color across every view it appears in.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand accent color competing with Apple System Blue — a second "important" color makes neither one mean anything.
Don't apply .glass-*/backdrop-filter to a plain content card or section — it's reserved for nav bars, dialogs, and popovers specifically.
Don't reach for warm/cream backgrounds, purple gradients, or heavy black borders — these read as generic "AI-generated" UI, the explicit anti-reference for this system.
Don't use a heavier shadow tier than the content needs just to make an ordinary card feel more prominent.
Don't invent a one-off radius value — every corner in the system derives from the single --radius primitive via the existing scale.
